ATTORNEY REVIEW ONLY — DO NOT SEND.

Public fact hook / hypothesis: Machina Labs is deploying cutting-edge AI-guided robotics for manufacturing (aerospace, defense, automotive) with multiple high-profile deployments and $170M+ in public funding. At this scale and with this level of technical complexity (robot foundation models, AI-driven process control, multi-material fabrication), there is likely significant IP documentation activity — but also significant risk around human-contribution attribution, AI-assisted invention records, trade-secret vs patent strategy, and disclosure timing as the company scales toward production and potential M&A. The AI Patent Strategy Scorecard could help the leadership team map their IP posture before the next funding or customer milestone.
Suggested lead magnet: AI Patent Strategy Scorecard — /ai-patent-strategy-scorecard
LinkedIn awareness draft exists for internal review only; do not post or tag without exact approval.

Internal LinkedIn awareness draft:
Companies building AI-guided robotics are running into a hidden IP challenge:

The AI doesn't file the patent. The human contribution does.

And when the system itself generates designs, optimizes processes, and controls fabrication — the documentation gap widens fast.

It's not just about what the robot makes.

It's about who designed the design process, what the AI contributed, and whether the company can later prove inventive conception.

For #founders and #CTOs: invention records are becoming a product operating system.
For #investors: IP diligence on physical-AI companies is increasingly about documentation, not just demos.
For #engineering-leaders: R&D speed and IP strategy need to move together — not later.
